_comment: SHARED FIXTURE (NRM-3) — two independent implementations must agree on this document.
Rust  : nmts/crypto/tests/api.rs            (what the standalone recovery tool parses)
Keys beginning with _ are documentation and are ignored by both parsers.
WHAT NRM-3 ADDS, and why this fixture exists beside nrm2-sample.json rather than replacing
it: a manifest is written in two places and they are not the same document twice. The FILE a
person downloads is built after an upload finished, so every blob it names already exists —
that document is still NRM-2 and every recovery tool ever shipped reads it. The
STORAGE-NETWORK copy is written INTO the quilt it describes, and a quilt's blob id is a hash
of its contents, this document included, so the writer cannot name it. The own-quilt form is
how that is said: 'my patch is called X, in the quilt you found this document in'.
This document therefore mixes BOTH forms on purpose — one item from an earlier upload whose
quilt is named outright, and one from the very upload this manifest is riding in. A reader
that resolves only one of the two passes half of a recovery and fails the other half years
later, which is exactly the failure the fixture is here to make loud now.
Note the own-quilt item has exactly ONE part and that part carries NO blob_id: a quilted item
is one patch in one blob, and naming a blob would contradict the form's whole meaning. Both
sides must REFUSE a document that breaks either rule.
